biography: Born in Bologna, Roberto Ravaglia's motorsport journey began not on the track, but amidst the roaring engines of his father's motorcycle repair shop. The smell of gasoline and the sight of finely tuned machines ignited a passion that quickly outgrew two wheels. He transitioned to karting at 14, displaying a natural aggression and uncanny ability to find the limit. A defining moment came during a regional karting championship when, despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, Ravaglia clawed his way to victory, overtaking the leader on the final corner with a daring move that became his trademark. After dominating Italian Formula Three, he caught the eye of Team DT Racing, quickly becoming a rising star in the touring car scene before his move to McLaren's F1 GTR program. Now at 27, Ravaglia is in his prime, known for his relentless pursuit of victory and an unwavering confidence that borders on arrogance.
drivingStyle: Ravaglia's driving style is characterized by a fearless, almost reckless approach. He attacks corners with an unmatched ferocity, often pushing the car beyond its perceived limits. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers to extract maximum performance in short bursts, relying on his raw speed to compensate. Under pressure, Ravaglia thrives, relishing the challenge of wheel-to-wheel combat. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and his ability to intimidate opponents with his aggressive positioning on the track.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their Formula Three days, fueled by contrasting driving styles – Rossi's calculated precision versus Ravaglia's raw aggression.

famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the Italian Touring Car Championship in 2022, dominating the season with a string of pole positions and race victories, solidifying his reputation as Italy's top touring car driver.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 1997 Spa 24 Hours with the McLaren F1 GTR due to excessive aggression in wet conditions, costing his team a likely victory.
